name: Stage 37:1: Nävekvarn to Kärrgruvorna
description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 37:1, Nävekvarn to Kärrgruvorna.
utilities: Nävekvarn/Gula Kvarn is the official start, with parking, bus 561 toward Nyköping, and nearby harbour/camping/food/lodging services. Hyttvallen IP/Nävekvarns IP is a useful alternate start-side access point for the rerouted approach.

Kärrgruvorna has parking at/near Blombergstorp, a shelter/fireplace/toilet/water cluster, information boards, and onward connection to stage 37:2. End-side buses are available from Skräddarstugan/Laggarbo/Syrtorpsvägen, but they are not at the shelter and service should be verified.
Nyköping C is the nearest practical rail anchor, far from both ends; use bus, taxi, bike, or pickup for the trailheads.
waterSources: Kärrgruvan spring is the only verified on-stage water source, near the end of the stage. Treat/filter/boil because Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality; a June 2025 hiker report found the level very low.
Nävekvarn harbour/camping water is useful before starting, but it is service/seasonal context rather than an on-trail natural source.
Stordammen, Lilldammen/Nyhyttan and other historic dam waters are industrial/natural water context only; do not list them as potable refills.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden distance is 8 km. Naturkartan shows 7.2 km in visible metadata but also exposes 8466 m, the 2025 long-distance passport lists 7.5 km, third-party/blog sources run around 8.0-8.5 km, and the current local route geometry measures about 6.9 km. Keep the official 8 km while flagging the mapped line as shorter than the currently signed reroute may be.
This is an inland branch from Nävekvarn to Kärrgruvorna, not the coastal main continuation. It connects from the Nävekvarn/stage 37 area to stage 37:2 at Kärrgruvorna.

No current formal fault report was found on the stage page during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Official comments say the stage was partly rerouted in 2023 from Nävekvarn toward Koppartorpsvägen; follow orange arrows from Gula Kvarn via Hyttvallen and Utsiktstornet. Alstorpsdammen is now described as a loop, not the main route.

Third-party GPX/app data can still show the old Nävekvarn/Alstorpsdammen line. A March 2025 user report and wider AllTrails loop reviews describe old/disused lines after Nävekvarn as hard to follow, wet, marshy, and blocked by windthrow/root plates; use current orange markings on the ground.

Geometry/topology: the local app route measures about 6.86 km and OSM relation 9631219 about 7.09 km, shorter than official/Naturkartan/passport values. Keep 8 km as the planning distance, flag the current drawn line as shorter than the signed Hyttvallen reroute may be, and snap the end to OSM node 5486317989 shared with stage 37:2.

If OSM relation 9631219 is used directly, exclude or repair its tiny disconnected 9 m fragment near 58.6413,16.7957. At the start, treat the Nävekvarn/Gula Kvarn area as a shared junction cluster with stage 37 rather than requiring exact node identity.
Route character: mining/cultural-history branch with forest roads/paths, dams and old industrial remains, a steep Kungstorpsberget section, then the shelter and mine-hole landscape at Kärrgruvorna.

Kungstorpsberget has a strenuous climb and exposed viewpoint terrain around Utsiktstornet at about 58.641892,16.819528; official text says to be careful with children. Hiker reports mention steep rope, stair or railing-assisted sections around the tower/descent area.

Kärrgruvorna contains more than 40 old mine openings over roughly 600 x 300 m, plus ruins, spoil heaps, water-filled holes and cultural remains. Stay on marked paths/boards, keep children and dogs controlled, avoid edges, shafts, snow/leaf-covered depressions and degraded covers, and do not disturb heritage features.

Kärrgruvan shelter is the strongest overnight infrastructure on the stage. No separate verified tent site was found; use allemansrätten carefully and avoid homes, farmland, mine holes, ruins, and sensitive cultural remains.

Use only prepared fireplaces. The official page specifically notes that a 2019 forest fire started near the Kärrgruvan shelter, so extinguish completely and check current fire bans before lighting anything. Firewood is not reliable; a June 2025 field note reported none available.
Kärrgruvan runt is a short easy loop at the endpoint and should appear as a local option once the user selects the Kärrgruvorna end area.
